canonical_statement: The study aimed to develop and evaluate explainable machine-learning models that predict anti-factor Xa range during unfractionated heparin therapy in critically ill patients to support dose adjustment.
This was a single-center retrospective cohort study using the Rennes University Hospital clinical data warehouse.
Eligible ICU stays occurred in medical, surgical, or cardiac surgery ICUs between December 21, 2019 and November 22, 2021.
Patients younger than 18 years were excluded.

Anti-Xa intervals were excluded when patients had recent protamine sulfate, subcutaneous UFH, low-molecular-weight heparin, direct oral anticoagulants, or antithrombin within the specified lookback windows.

population.label: Candidate anti-Xa intervals
exclusion_criteria: Subcutaneous UFH or LMWH within 48 h
Direct oral anticoagulant or antithrombin within 7 days

canonical_statement: Intervals between consecutive anti-Xa assays shorter than 6 hours or longer than 48 hours were excluded.
Intervals with missing anti-Xa results or remaining missing predictor data after the study preprocessing rules were excluded.

population.label: Candidate anti-Xa intervals
exclusion_criteria: Missing required predictor data after preprocessing

canonical_statement: The predicted anti-Xa outcome was categorized as sub-therapeutic below 0.3, therapeutic from 0.3 to 0.7, and supra-therapeutic above 0.7.
Anti-Xa activity was measured on fresh citrated plasma using the STA Liquid Anti-Xa chromogenic assay with dedicated calibrators and controls on STA R Max 2 instrumentation.

Sixteen routinely collected predictors were used, spanning age, sex, BMI, ECMO, urine output, creatinine, renal replacement therapy, fibrinogen, hemoglobin, hematocrit, bilirubin, UFH dosing and boluses, prior anti-Xa, and interval duration.
Urine output and UFH boluses were summed over each interval, whereas other continuous predictors were averaged over the interval.
Intervals with missing demographic features or UFH infusion rates were excluded.
Missing laboratory results were imputed by linear interpolation.
Continuous variables were normalized, categorical variables were one-hot encoded, and right-skewed variables were log-transformed and normalized.
The six evaluated classifiers were random forest, linear SVM, radial-basis-function SVM, XGBoost, neural network, and penalized logistic regression.
Hyperparameter search used Latin hypercube sampling and model selection used ten-fold stratified cross-validation.
Seventy percent of anti-Xa intervals were assigned to model training and 30% to the test set.
Hyperparameters were selected using the best cross-validated AUROC.

Because the supra-therapeutic class was relatively rare, case weights were used where supported to give equal total weight to each class; this was available only for penalized logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost.
The investigators did not apply a model-calibration method.
Model evaluation included AUROC, AUPRC, accuracy, F1 score, sensitivity, specificity, and calibration plots.
Overall multiclass AUROC used the Hand and Till method, and overall AUPRC used macro averaging.
Of 7,488 screened anti-Xa intervals, 3,790 intervals were included in the final analysis.
The final cohort comprised 211 critically ill patients contributing 286 ICU stays and 3,790 anti-Xa intervals.

population.label: Critically ill patients receiving UFH with included anti-Xa intervals

canonical_statement: The final patient cohort was 78% male (165 of 211 patients).
Median age in the final patient cohort was 66.0 years with an interquartile range of 54.0 to 72.0 years.

population.label: Final patient cohort; median age 66.0 years [54.0-72.0]

canonical_statement: Median BMI in the final patient cohort was 27.6 kg/m² with an interquartile range of 23.8 to 31.2 kg/m².

population.label: Final patient cohort; median BMI 27.6 kg/m² [23.8-31.2]

canonical_statement: During the included ICU stays, median admission SOFA score was 11 [8-13], 92% of patients received mechanical ventilation during the ICU stay, and 24% received ECMO.

population.label: Included ICU stays with high acuity; median SOFA 11 [8-13], 92% mechanical ventilation, 24% ECMO

canonical_statement: Median ICU length of stay among included stays was 16.3 days [8.6-31.1].

population.label: Included ICU stays; median length of stay 16.3 days [8.6-31.1]

canonical_statement: The training set contained 2,652 anti-Xa intervals and the test set contained 1,138 anti-Xa intervals.
The authors reported no statistically significant differences in the measured feature distributions between the training and test sets.

Given 279 ICU stays represented in the training set, 224 in the test set, and 286 unique included ICU stays overall, at least 217 ICU stays must have contributed intervals to both sets (279 + 224 - 286 = 217).
XGBoost achieved a mean cross-validated AUROC of 0.79 [0.76-0.82].
Penalized logistic regression achieved a mean cross-validated AUROC of 0.79 [0.77-0.81].
Penalized logistic regression achieved a mean cross-validated AUPRC of 0.57 [0.54-0.60].
Random forest achieved a mean cross-validated AUPRC of 0.57 [0.55-0.59].
Neural network achieved a mean cross-validated AUPRC of 0.57 [0.55-0.58].
Random forest achieved test-set AUROC of 0.80 [0.77-0.83].
XGBoost achieved test-set AUROC of 0.80 [0.76-0.83].
Random forest achieved test-set AUPRC of 0.61 [0.58-0.65].
Neural network achieved test-set accuracy of 0.74 [0.71-0.76].
Neural network achieved test-set F1 score of 0.76 [0.73-0.78].
Random forest achieved test-set sensitivity of 0.56 [0.53-0.59].
Random forest achieved test-set specificity of 0.82 [0.82-0.82].
Random forest achieved test-set accuracy of 0.71 [0.68-0.73].
Random forest achieved test-set F1 score of 0.57 [0.53-0.61].
Calibration was described as good for infra-therapeutic-versus-others and normal-versus-others predictions but low for supra-therapeutic-versus-others predictions.
For models with feature-importance outputs, the current UFH rate, prior UFH rate, and start-of-interval anti-Xa were the most important predictors.
Forty-nine percent of anti-Xa results in the whole cohort were below 0.3 and therefore classified as infra-therapeutic.
Fifty-four percent of first anti-Xa results were below 0.3 and therefore classified as infra-therapeutic.

canonical_statement: The authors proposed that the developed models could function as clinical decision support to help clinicians select UFH doses likely to reach the target anti-Xa range more quickly.
The study was single-center, limiting generalizability to other hospitals.
The authors considered the sample size small and noted that it could affect model accuracy.
The retrospective dataset did not provide thrombotic or hemorrhagic clinical outcomes.
Because the models require a start-of-interval anti-Xa value, they are not suitable for selecting the initial UFH dose before any anti-Xa measurement.
The supra-therapeutic class was relatively rare, and despite case weighting the models had limited performance for supra-therapeutic predictions.
The models did not include antithrombin levels, which the authors identified as potentially important for ECMO patients with heparin resistance.

The authors concluded that machine-learning models showed good performance for predicting anti-Xa results during UFH therapy, but prospective multicenter validation is needed before clinical integration.
